definitions.explanation: A musical composition designed to develop a specific technical skill in performance. While primarily a practice piece, many étude are also performed in concerts as standalone works of artistic merit.

examples.japanese: ショパンの{演習曲|えんしゅうきょく}を{練習|れんしゅう}している。
この{演習曲|えんしゅうきょく}は{指|ゆび}の{独立|どくりつ}を{鍛|きた}えるのに{適|てき}している。
examples.english: This étude is suitable for training finger independence.

examples.japanese: ピアノの{演習曲|えんしゅうきょく}には、チェルニーやハノンのように{技術的|ぎじゅつてき}な{訓練|くんれん}を{目的|もくてき}としたものが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Among piano études, many are aimed at technical training, such as those by Czerny and Hanon.

notes:
A compound of {演習|えんしゅう} (practice, exercise) and {曲|きょく} (musical piece). The loanword エチュード (from French étude) is also widely used, especially in conversational contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ピアノの{演習曲|えんしゅうきょく} — piano étude
- {演習曲|えんしゅうきょく}を{弾|ひ}く — to play an étude
- {演習曲|えんしゅうきょく}{集|しゅう} — collection of études

FAMOUS EXAMPLES:
- ショパンの{演習曲|えんしゅうきょく} — Chopin's Études (Op. 10, Op. 25), considered masterpieces of both technical challenge and musical beauty
- チェルニー — Czerny, composer of fundamental piano exercises
- ハノン — Hanon, known for systematic finger exercises
- リストの{超絶技巧|ちょうぜつぎこう}{演習曲|えんしゅうきょく} — Liszt's Transcendental Études

RELATED WORDS:
- エチュード — étude (loanword from French, interchangeable in music contexts)
- {練習曲|れんしゅうきょく} — practice piece (synonym, sometimes used interchangeably)
- {教則本|きょうそくぼん} — instruction book, method book (a book of graded exercises)
